front: A sale posts to which two accounts before any tax?
back: Debtors (asset) debit and Sales (income) credit; tax adds a liability, it is never income. (Receivable up, income up, tax owed)

front: You posted the same invoice twice. What does the trial balance show?
back: It still balances. A double posting is wrong but symmetric, so only the ledger or a report catches it. (Balance is not correctness)

front: Why is SST a liability rather than a cost?
back: The customer paid it to you on the government's behalf, so you hold it until the return is filed. (You are the collection agent)

front: Which three books does one transaction touch?
back: General ledger for worth and profit, payment ledger for settlement, stock ledger for quantity and value. (Three ledgers, one voucher)

front: When is a Journal Entry the right document?
back: When no business document exists: accrual, depreciation, correction or opening balance. Never for a sale or a purchase. (Adjustment, not trade)

front: Which documents change stock quantity?
back: Purchase Receipt, Delivery Note, Stock Entry and Stock Reconciliation, and only once submitted. (Not invoices, not payments)

front: Why does one product have four prices?
back: Four channels with different economics: each channel is a price list plus its own rules, not a reporting label. (A channel is economics)

front: How is a reorder point calculated?
back: Average daily demand times lead time, plus safety stock for demand and supply variability. (Demand times wait, plus buffer)

front: Gross margin or net margin, what is the difference?
back: Gross is selling price less landed cost; net also absorbs discounts, freight out and overheads. (Landed cost first, then everything)

front: What breaks when a partial delivery becomes a second order?
back: The order book doubles, fill rate collapses and the same stock is promised twice. (One order, many deliveries)

front: What does saving a draft change in the stock and the books?
back: Nothing. No stock ledger entry and no general ledger row exists until the document is submitted, so drafts are invisible to reports. (Draft is a proposal)

front: Why can a submitted document not simply be deleted?
back: Its stock and ledger rows are already posted. Cancelling writes offsetting rows and keeps the record, which is what an auditor needs to see. (Reverse, never remove)

front: What must happen before a document can be amended?
back: It must be cancelled first. Amend then creates a new document carrying amended_from, while the original stays cancelled and untouched. (Cancel, then amend)

front: What does the error Active Referencing Documents tell you to do?
back: A submitted document points at this one, so cancel from the bottom of the chain upwards: invoice first, then delivery note. (Unwind downward)

front: Which single report check proves a posting really happened?
back: Open the Stock Ledger and the General Ledger filtered by the voucher. If the rows are there, the document posted; if not, it is still a draft. (Follow the voucher)

front: Which control reaches every DocType, document and report from one field?
back: The awesome bar at the top of the Desk. Two letters and Enter open a doctype list; a document name jumps straight to the record. (One box to rule them)

front: What makes a saved filter more useful than a custom report?
back: It is configuration, so it survives upgrades, respects user permissions and can be changed by the client without a developer. (No code to maintain)

front: Why will the same saved view show different rows to two users?
back: Saved filters are shared, but user permissions restrict which records each person may see, so the row count differs by role. (Permissions narrow rows)

front: When is Report Builder the wrong tool?
back: When the question needs joins across DocTypes or logic that SQL cannot express. That is a Query or Script Report, and you will maintain it. (One doctype only)

front: What is the fastest way to prove a report total is right?
back: Reproduce the same filter in the list view and compare the record count and the total. The list shows its filters; the report hides them. (Count the rows)

front: Which five root groups must a new company show?
back: Application of Funds, Sources of Funds, Equity, Income and Expenses. A missing group means the template did not load. (Count them in the tree)

front: Why never rename the standard account tree?
back: Reports and tax templates look accounts up by name, so renaming breaks every report the client will ever ask for. (Add leaves, keep nodes)

front: Where do rounding differences land?
back: The Round Off account set in company defaults, never in the customer's receivable. (One account, named once)

front: Do cost centres change the trial balance?
back: No. A dimension splits a posting for analysis while the total stays exactly the same. (Analysis, not amount)

front: A 1,200.00 net invoice at SST 10 per cent, what are tax and total?
back: 120.00 tax and 1,320.00 grand total. Predict it before the invoice is saved. (The course anchor numbers)

front: One box equals twelve pieces. What does a receipt of 1 Box post?
back: A stock balance of 12 Nos, because every stock row and valuation runs in the stock UOM. (Convert before you count)

front: What must every warehouse point at?
back: A stock account through the company defaults, so valuation has somewhere to post. (A location with a ledger)

front: Role permission or user permission, which one wins?
back: The narrower of the two: the role grants the action, the user permission filters the rows. (Do versus see)

front: The valuation method was wrong since go live. What is the honest fix?
back: Repost Item Valuation, not an edit. The method itself is set per company and is not a per document choice. (Repost, do not retype)

front: Which three things are verified before anyone is allowed to transact?
back: Company and abbreviation against registration documents, currency and fiscal year, then the chart of accounts. (Paper first)

front: What does Maintain Stock switched off mean?
back: The item never touches the stock ledger, though it can still be bought and sold as a service. (The gate before all four)

front: Serial or batch, and when?
back: Serial for units traced individually such as warranty appliances, batch for quantities made or received together with expiry. (One unit, one lot)

front: An item has no Item Price record for the list. What rate loads?
back: Zero, and the document will post at zero unless someone reads the rate before submitting. (A missing record means free goods)

front: Which mechanism turns 216.00 into 205.20?
back: A pricing rule applying five per cent, resolved after the item price sets the base rate. (Rule overrides price)

front: Why is the stock UOM special?
back: Every stock ledger row, Bin and valuation figure is kept in it, and other UOMs are only conversions of it. (Valuation's native language)

front: Where does a quotation's price list come from?
back: The customer's default price list, after which a pricing rule may override the rate on the line. (Defaults cascade)

front: Why is an address a separate document?
back: One party can hold billing, shipping and contact addresses, and each document picks the one it needs. (One record per role)

front: Item Price or Pricing Rule?
back: An item price states this item on this list at this rate from this date; a rule tests conditions and overrides it. (Fact versus override)

front: Ten units for a dealer at 216.00 less five per cent?
back: 205.20 per unit, so 2,052.00 net before tax. (The chapter anchor)

front: What do supplier payment terms actually drive?
back: The payment schedule on the bill, and therefore the payment run and the ageing buckets. (Schedule, not text)

front: What does submitting a quotation change?
back: Nothing in the ledger and nothing in stock. It is an offer with a validity date. (A promise writes nothing)

front: Which document posts cost of goods sold?
back: The Delivery Note, using the valuation the stock ledger already holds, not the invoice. (The physical event)

front: Five units leave Main Warehouse at 120.00. What is cost of goods sold?
back: 600.00, and Stock Balance then shows zero with no negative quantity anywhere. (Quantity times valuation rate)

front: Why convert the invoice from the delivery note?
back: So billed quantity equals dispatched quantity and the order does not stay open as to bill. (Match paper to goods)

front: What makes a payment entry clear an invoice?
back: Allocation. Cash without allocation leaves the invoice open and the customer looking like a debtor. (Allocate or it did not happen)

front: Two of five units are delivered. What does the order show?
back: Partly delivered with three pending, while stock falls by two and the remaining three stay in the warehouse. (One order, one truth)

front: Ten per cent off 1,200.00 gives which three numbers?
back: 1,080.00 net, 108.00 SST and 1,188.00 total. (Tax follows the net)

front: How is a credit note created?
back: As a return against the original invoice, so stock, revenue and tax all reverse together. (Never a negative invoice)

front: Where is credit checking switched on?
back: Selling Settings once, after which the limit itself lives on the customer record. (Setting, then party)

front: Which three reports close a sales month?
back: General ledger by party, payment ledger and aged receivables, and they must agree before anyone says done. (Three views, one number)

front: Which purchase document moves stock?
back: The Purchase Receipt. It debits stock and credits an interim stock account, so no profit appears yet. (Balance sheet only)

front: What does the three way match compare?
back: Quantity, rate and total across order, receipt and bill, and a mismatch is what blocks or flags the bill. (Order, goods, bill)

front: What goes wrong when you bill without receiving?
back: The interim stock account never clears and no stock arrives, yet the liability exists for goods you do not hold. (The optional step is not free)

front: Which three numbers are read before a purchase order is submitted?
back: Net total, tax and grand total, each equal to the sum of the lines. (Read, then submit)

front: What makes a supplier payment settle the bill?
back: Allocation against the purchase invoice. The payment entry alone only moves cash. (Same rule as sales)

front: One damaged unit goes back to the supplier. In what order?
back: The goods return first, then the bill adjustment, so stock and tax reverse together. (Reverse, then bill)

front: How is an advance to a supplier recorded?
back: A payment entry with no allocation against an invoice, so it stays a liability rather than an expense. (Money before paper)

front: Where does inbound freight belong?
back: In a Landed Cost Voucher, allocated across the received units and revaluing the stock they sit in. (Into stock, not expense)

front: What must be true after a landed cost allocation?
back: The downstream margin reports actually use the new valuation, otherwise the allocation is decoration. (Revaluation must be read)

front: What do ageing buckets tell you?
back: When money leaves, not whether the bill is correct. Correctness is the three way match. (Timing, not truth)

front: How many stock ledger rows does a transfer create?
back: Two, an outgoing and an incoming row at the same rate, written by one voucher. (In and out, one document)

front: What corrects a count difference?
back: A Stock Reconciliation with the counted quantity, including counts that are zero. (Truth on paper)

front: Which three numbers must agree after any movement?
back: Bin quantity, the stock ledger running total and the Stock Balance report. (Three views of one number)

front: Reorder level or reorder quantity?
back: The level triggers the alert, the quantity is how much the suggestion orders. (When versus how much)

front: Does reserving stock for a work order move the ledger?
back: No. Reserved quantity is planning only, and only a Stock Entry moves stock. (Plan versus post)

front: Which layer does a sale consume under FIFO?
back: The oldest remaining layer, at that layer's own rate. (First in, first costed)

front: Receipts at 100 and 120, then one unit sold. What is the cost?
back: 100, because the oldest layer leaves first and 120 stays in stock. (Queue, not average)

front: How is a wrong valuation corrected?
back: Repost Item Valuation. A journal would create a second version of the truth beside the ledger. (Recalculate history)

front: What does negative stock do to valuation?
back: It guesses a rate, usually the last known, so cost of goods sold and stock value both drift. (A guess dressed as a number)

front: Which three figures must agree?
back: Stock Balance quantity, the stock ledger value and the stock account in the general ledger. (Quantity, history, value)

front: What is the measurable business case for scanning on the warehouse floor?
back: Variance and write-off value, measured before and after. Speed is nice; a distributor that stops writing off stock has a number finance will defend. (Variance, not romance)

front: Why must the barcode list be checked for duplicates before go-live?
back: A code pointing at two items resolves silently to one of them, so both count wrong and no error is raised at the scanner. (One code, one item)

front: What turns a count difference into an auditable event?
back: The signed count sheet, the device export with user and timestamp, and the reconciliation voucher that carries both as attachments. (Sheet, export, voucher)

front: What must be proved about a device that queues scans offline?
back: That the voucher total equals the device total, and that a repeated sync with the same reference is refused rather than posted twice. (Send it twice)

front: How is a recount threshold best expressed?
back: In money per line, with a second counter above it and a named approver, because value is what the write-off costs. (Money, not units)

front: When does an accrual reverse?
back: On the reversal date set when it was posted, so the actual invoice lands cleanly in the next period. (Decide the date at posting time)

front: What is a prepayment before it is consumed?
back: An asset: cover that has been paid for but not yet used. (Asset until used)

front: What does a clean bank reconciliation prove?
back: That every statement line is matched to the ledger, so cash for the period is fully explained with no plug. (No suspense account)

front: How is a submitted journal corrected?
back: Reverse it, or cancel and amend, because the trail is the whole point. (History is append only)

front: Which four journal situations recur monthly?
back: Accrual, prepayment release, depreciation and correction. (The monthly four)

front: What is the most common month end failure?
back: Closing with unposted documents: drafts, unallocated payments and negative stock. (Check before you close)

front: What does the Period Closing Voucher actually do?
back: It zeroes income and expense accounts into the closing account and leaves balance sheet accounts alone. (Profit and loss to zero)

front: Can a document be edited in a closed period?
back: Not without reopening or correcting in the next period. The close is a lock, not a label. (Lock, do not argue)

front: At year end, what carries forward?
back: Every balance sheet balance, while the profit and loss closes into equity. (Balances yes, profit no)

front: Who signs a close off?
back: Every row of the close calendar needs an owner and a proof, and the pack must read without the system. (Names and evidence)

front: What has to exist before anyone applies for leave?
back: The holiday list for the current and next year, the leave types with their entitlement, and the approver rule. Otherwise the first public holiday eats an entitlement. (Calendar first)

front: Which four employee fields does payroll actually read?
back: Joining date, department, the statutory identifiers (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, tax number) and bank details. Everything else is context. (Date, department, IDs, bank)

front: Why does leave without pay have to reach payroll?
back: Because an unpaid day that never becomes a deduction is a salary overpayment the employee spots before the consultant does. (Payroll input)

front: What do the four pre-payroll checks cover?
back: Headcount name by name against the payroll list, record completeness, leave balances against policy, and advances cleared or explained. (Half an hour)

front: How should the HR app installation be handled?
back: As a maintenance change: backup first, ask the host to fetch and install the app, migrate, open every new document, then record the versions. (Host, backup, evidence)

front: What are the five outputs a payroll month must produce?
back: Payslips, a payroll register, the salary journal, the statutory remittances, and data sufficient for the annual earnings statement. (Five, every month)

front: Why is the journal larger than net pay?
back: Because gross includes employer EPF, SOCSO and EIS shares as extra expense, while net pay is gross minus the employee's deductions only. (Employer shares)

front: What belongs in the income tax setup, and what must be dated?
back: The published brackets, reliefs and rebates from the current schedule — and a dated note of the source and who confirmed it. (Configure, don't advise)

front: What proves a payroll month is finished?
back: Register equals journal, four statutory liabilities at zero after remittance, salary payable cleared, headcount agreed, and the month filed. (Four checks)

front: How is a leaver's final month assembled?
back: Prorate from the relieving date, encash remaining leave, clear advances, then pay — and close the employee record with a date. (Prorate, encash, clear, pay)

front: Does a work order move stock?
back: No, it reserves. Only the transfer and the manufacture entry move quantity. (Promise versus movement)

front: What is work in progress?
back: The value of components consumed but not yet finished, sitting in the work in progress warehouse. (Half made stock)

front: What does a BOM cost roll up contain?
back: Material cost plus operating cost per unit, at the BOM's own rates and operations. (Material plus operations)

front: Where are components actually consumed?
back: In the Manufacture stock entry, which also produces and values the finished item. (One document, two directions)

front: Why must the finished valuation be explainable?
back: It becomes the cost of every later sale, so an unexplainable BOM cost is an unexplainable margin. (Cost in, cost out)

front: How is cost per finished unit calculated?
back: Materials plus operations, divided by good units, with scrap in the numerator and never quietly subtracted. (Divide by good units)

front: One of ten units is scrapped. What happens to total cost?
back: It stays the same and the nine good units carry it, so unit cost rises. (Spread, not lost)

front: How is scrap recorded?
back: As a quantity on the manufacture entry or a separate scrap entry, not as a journal. (Quantity, not money)

front: How many movements does subcontracting create?
back: Three: material out to the subcontractor, the service received, and the finished material back. (Out, service, back)

front: Where must production cost land?
back: In inventory value. An expense account here means the stock was under costed. (Balance sheet first)

front: Why is a project profit and loss empty?
back: Something was posted without the project field, because the collector only sees postings that name it. (Name it or lose it)

front: Where does project revenue come from?
back: Sales invoices that name the project, not quotations and not orders. (Invoices, not promises)

front: What does a timesheet carry besides hours?
back: A billing rate and a costing rate, so one hour is both revenue and cost. (Two rates, one hour)

front: Why invoice from the timesheet?
back: Hours, rate and project land on the invoice without retyping, so the margin stays traceable. (No retyping)

front: What does closing a project do?
back: It stops further time and cost postings, and it does not reverse revenue already billed. (Stop, do not undo)

front: How is a van capitalised rather than expensed?
back: With a purchase invoice whose item is marked as a fixed asset, which creates the Asset record. (Asset item, not expense)

front: Where does accumulated depreciation have to agree?
back: In three places: the asset register, the depreciation account in the ledger and the schedule. (Three views, one number)

front: Lead or opportunity?
back: A lead is an unqualified contact, an opportunity is a deal with a value, a date and a probability. (Contact versus deal)

front: How is weighted pipeline calculated?
back: Sum of value times probability across all open opportunities. (Value times confidence)

front: When does a quality inspection happen?
back: On receipt, before the goods become available stock, when the item is configured that way. (Before it is stock)

front: Which five fields make an issue defensible later?
back: Asset, symptom, reporter, priority and promised response, plus the resolution note on close. Everything else is optional. (Five, every time)

front: Why do service levels breach themselves over a long weekend?
back: Because the clock runs on the service calendar. If working hours and holidays are not configured, a Friday evening issue breaches by Monday morning. (Calendar, not effort)

front: What decides whether a repair is free of charge?
back: The serial's delivery date against the warranty period, the exclusions in the agreement, and the evidence attached at logging. The decision and its reason are recorded. (Date, serial, evidence)

front: Why is a replacement the riskiest of the three service outcomes?
back: Because it needs a delivery out and the old unit back in. If the return is forgotten, a serial that no longer exists stays in stock forever. (Two documents)

front: Which four numbers belong in the monthly service pack?
back: Open issues by priority, median response and resolution per priority, warranty cost versus revenue per model, and billable versus absorbed hours. (Queue, clock, cost, hours)

front: What must a Malaysian tax invoice show?
back: Company name, registration number and SST number, plus the tax breakdown per line. (Not optional)

front: What do auditors ask about numbering first?
back: Whether there are gaps or duplicates in the series, and who can edit the prefix. (Series integrity)

front: Why does a notification fire twice?
back: It is attached to more than one event, or its condition matches both a draft and a submit. (One event, one send)

front: What should never be customised with code in this volume?
back: Anything the print format builder or notification fields already do, because code does not survive an upgrade. (Configuration survives)

front: How is a print format tested?
back: With a real submitted document carrying real tax and a real address, never with a blank form. (Real document, real state)

front: How do you tell whether a request is configuration or development?
back: If it can be made and reversed in the browser without a file or a deployment, it is configuration and it is yours. Otherwise it belongs to a developer. (Reversible without a deploy)

front: What does a property setter leave untouched underneath?
back: The standard DocType definition. The override sits on top, so a migration replaces the standard and keeps the setter. (Override, not edit)

front: Which custom DocType decision is hardest to undo and why?
back: The naming series. Every record name is referenced by links, so renumbering later breaks them. Decide before the first save. (Names are forever)

front: When does a table field beat a long text field?
back: When somebody will count, sum or report per line, such as findings by severity. Rows can be reported; prose cannot. (Count it or drop it)

front: What must the change register carry besides the change itself?
back: The reason it was made, who asked for it, the date, and how to reverse it — plus a copy held outside the system. (Why and how to undo)

front: Role permission or user permission, what is the difference?
back: A role grants actions on a DocType, a user permission filters the records, and the narrower wins. (Do versus see)

front: How is a user kept to one warehouse?
back: With a user permission on Warehouse for that user, not with a new role. (Row filter)

front: What makes a discount workflow correct?
back: A low discount flows straight to submitted while a high one waits at pending approval for the right role. (States and transitions)

front: When is auto repeat safe?
back: For genuinely recurring documents with a fixed shape, never for ones a human must judge. (Rhythm, not judgement)

front: What does an access review check?
back: That every active login still matches a job, quarterly, including the ones nobody uses. (Quarterly ritual)

front: Why one template per rate per direction?
back: The posting account and the return box differ by direction, and mixing them makes the return untraceable. (Account and box)

front: Goods at ten per cent and services at eight per cent on one invoice?
back: Two lines on two templates, each rate posting to its own account. (Never one line)

front: Item tax category or customer default, which applies?
back: The item's category wins, which is useful for exempt goods and dangerous when unintended. (Product beats party)

front: Which documents feed the SST-02 return?
back: Posted invoices only, because drafts, cancelled documents and unsubmitted returns are excluded. (Posted only)

front: Which three numbers must agree?
back: The return figure, the tax summary by account and the ledger balance of the tax account. (One number, three views)

front: What does a submission return?
back: A submission ID, an accepted list carrying validation identifiers, and a rejected list with reasons. (One ID and two lists)

front: How long is the cancellation window?
back: 72 hours after validation, after which only a credit or debit note can correct the document. (72, not 24)

front: What are document types 01 to 04?
back: Invoice, credit note, debit note and refund note. (Four types)

front: When is consolidation allowed?
back: For many small sales to the general public grouped into one monthly e-Invoice, not for business buyers. (Consumer sales only)

front: What must the finance team be able to see?
back: One board showing pending, accepted, rejected and cancelled documents, with the reason for each rejection. (Status board)

front: What must the mapping workbook contain?
back: Every old value with a new target, an owner and a decision date, signed before the import starts. (A written agreement)

front: Why import in dependency order?
back: ERPNext refuses children without parents, so the order is the data model rather than a preference. (Parents first)

front: How are opening balances loaded?
back: As a single journal dated the day before go live, with a source document behind every figure. (One journal)

front: What proves an import is complete?
back: The log: rows attempted, created, updated and failed, plus a duplicate count. (The log is the evidence)

front: Which five checks come before anyone is allowed to transact?
back: Assets equal liabilities plus equity, the trial balance balances, stock ties to the count, debtors to statements, tax to returns. (Paper, then access)

front: What makes a UAT case pass?
back: The expected figure appears on screen, not merely that the screen did not produce an error. (Figures, not silence)

front: Why is cut over ordered rather than parallel?
back: Each step produces the input for the next, so reordering it creates work that must be redone. (Dependency, not convenience)

front: Which five numbers are measured daily in hypercare?
back: Tickets raised, invoices posted, stock errors, close progress and logins. (Five numbers a day)

front: What ends hypercare?
back: A go or no go decision on evidence where every criterion carries a number and someone signs it. (Decision on evidence)

front: What goes into the handover pack?
back: Configuration record, mapping workbook, UAT sign off, cut over log, open items and how to run the close. (The project's memory)

front: What two facts does a restore drill give the client?
back: That the backup actually restores, and how many minutes the business needs before it can trade again. Both belong in the handover pack. (Time it out loud)

front: Why does staging need a copy of production data?
back: Upgrades break on custom fields, print formats and workflow states, which live in the data and configuration rather than in the code. (Empty sites prove little)

front: What belongs in the version register?
back: The exact Frappe, ERPNext and custom app versions, pinned at go-live, with the date each was last confirmed and who confirmed it. (Numbers, dates, names)

front: Which five checks make up the post-upgrade verification?
back: Log in as a normal user, submit a test invoice, print it, run two saved reports, and submit one e-Invoice in sandbox. (Twenty minutes, five checks)

front: What makes a rollback plan usable rather than aspirational?
back: A backup taken minutes before the change, a named decision maker, a cut-off time, and a short recorded list of transactions to replay. (One name, one time)

front: Why is a shared login worse than a weak password?
back: Because it destroys the audit trail and makes a departure impossible to unwind. You cannot disable one person without disabling everyone. (One person, one account)

front: What evidence proves a restriction actually restricts?
back: A second login that shows the difference, or a refused connection from outside the network. Configuration alone is not evidence. (Two logins)

front: What must exist before two-factor is enforced for finance?
back: A tested recovery path and a second enrolled device, plus a recorded reset authority, so month end cannot be lost to a phone. (Recovery first)

front: How should integration keys and e-Invoice credentials be managed?
back: One key per integration, an owner and purpose in a register, storage outside documents, a rotation date, and a tested revocation. (One key, one job)

front: What are the first two moves in a suspected compromise?
back: Contain access — disable the account, revoke the key — then preserve the logs before anything is cleaned or restored. (Contain, preserve)

front: What three things shape a hypercare week?
back: A morning check with a name and time, same-day triage of anything wrong, and one written update per day. Everything else is optional. (Check, triage, update)

front: How should a fix list be split, and in what order?
back: Wrong numbers first, then blocked work, then cosmetic in one agreed batch — and publish the rule so volume does not decide. (Numbers before noise)

front: Why is the second-user test more valuable than a training record?
back: It measures capability: a non-champion completes a weekly cycle unaided while you watch in silence, exposing hesitations that training missed. (Watch, don't help)

front: Which five checks make up the weekly health routine?
back: Scheduled jobs ran, error log quiet, stock and ledger agree, aged drafts counted, backups completed — signed with a date and a name. (Fifteen minutes)

front: What does a good exit actually deliver?
back: Every open item closed as fixed, accepted or transferred, keys handed back, your access revoked, a named successor, and one dated optional review. (Capability, not farewell)
